claim: Storing weights, activations and gradients in fp16 nearly halves training memory versus fp32, which is the base saving every memory budget in this run starts from.
stance_target: The repo's bf16-everywhere policy and its 2-bytes-per-parameter weight term
scope_conditions: FP16 storage with an FP32 master copy; convolutional and recurrent networks across classification, regression and generative tasks
quoted_support: We introduce methodology for training deep neural networks using half-precision floating point numbers, without losing model accuracy or having to modify hyper-parameters. This nearly halves memory requirements and, on recent GPUs, speeds up arithmetic.

claim: An fp32 master copy of the weights is required: gradients are accumulated into a single-precision copy that is rounded to half precision for forward and backward, adding 4 bytes per parameter to the budget.
stance_target: The repo's 16-bytes-per-parameter figure for a fully trainable model (2 weights + 2 grads + 4 master + 8 Adam)
scope_conditions: FP16 training with FP32 master weights
quoted_support: Firstly, we recommend maintaining a single-precision copy of weights that accumulates the gradients after each optimizer step (this copy is rounded to half-precision for the forward- and back-propagation).

claim: Loss scaling is required to keep small-magnitude gradients from flushing to zero in fp16, and fp16 products must accumulate into fp32 outputs.
stance_target: The repo's use of bf16 rather than fp16, since bf16's wider exponent range removes the underflow problem
scope_conditions: FP16 training; loss scaling and FP32 accumulation
quoted_support: Since FP16 format has a narrower dynamic range than FP32, we introduce three techniques to prevent model accuracy loss: maintaining a master copy of weights in FP32, loss-scaling that minimizes gradient values becoming zeros, and FP16 arithmetic with accumulation in FP32.

claim: Half-precision arithmetic throughput is 2x to 8x higher than single precision on tensor-core GPUs, so reduced precision buys speed as well as memory.
stance_target: The repo's measured bf16 162 TFLOPS versus fp32 13 TFLOPS on the CMP 170HX
scope_conditions: GPUs with reduced-precision math units; general statement
quoted_support: For example, half-precision math throughput in recent GPUs is 2× to 8× higher than for single-precision.

claim: The recipe needs no changes to models or training hyperparameters and matches fp32 accuracy across image classification, generation, detection, language modeling, translation and speech.
stance_target: Whether switching the repo's baseline to bf16 autocast invalidates comparability with published numbers
scope_conditions: Convolutional and recurrent architectures; classification, regression and generative tasks
quoted_support: The proposed methodology requires no changes to models or training hyper-parameters.

claim: Reduced precision addresses memory bandwidth and arithmetic throughput but not latency, so it does not help a step that is bound by interconnect latency - which is the CMP 170HX box's actual constraint.
stance_target: Whether bf16 alone can rescue throughput on a PCIe Gen2 x4 fabric
scope_conditions: Performance limited by arithmetic bandwidth, memory bandwidth or latency
quoted_support: Performance (speed) of any program, including neural network training and inference, is limited by one of three factors: arithmetic bandwidth, memory bandwidth, or latency. Reduced precision addresses two of these limiters.
